subject: Geo-split billing & commit flexibility for AtlasAI
messages:
From: Elena Soto <esoto@atlasai.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: Marco Ruiz <mruiz@atlasai.com>
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing question — region splits & commit pooling

Hi Lauren / Rafael,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. We're pulling together final numbers for Q3 and have a few open items before we start a trial:

- Can Redwood apply a single annual commit across regions (US/EU/APAC) or do commits need to be region-specific?
- If commit pooling is supported, how are discounts and per-token tiers calculated when usage is cross-region (e.g., 60% US, 30% EU, 10% APAC)?
- Do you apply regional surcharges for APAC or EU? If so, can those be credited back if we later move to a dedicated instance in-region?
- Any precedent for providing retroactive credits if our final usage split ends up different than forecasted?

We attached our forecast and a short breakdown of traffic by region. Hoping to get a simple example (math) and a recommended packaging option (blended bucket vs. region-isolated commits). Also would like a short mutual action plan so we can align procurement timelines.

Attachments: [AtlasAI_traffic_forecast_May2025.xlsx (xlsx)]

Best,
Elena
Elena Soto
Head of Platform Partnerships | AtlasAI
elena.s@atlasai.com
From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <esoto@atlasai.com>
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 19 Jul 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing question — region splits & commit pooling

Elena — appreciate the clear ask and the forecast. Quick answers up-front: yes, we can support a pooled (single) commit for usage across regions with a couple of configuration options; APAC typically has a small surcharge unless the customer requests dedicated capacity in APAC.

I attached a short note with worked examples for a $2M annual commit with your 60/30/10 split and two packaging options:
- Blended bucket (single commit, blended per-token rate, regional multipliers applied at invoice time)
- Weighted buckets (one commit, commit allocation per region that can be rebalanced quarterly)

Highlights from the note (high level):
- Blended bucket gives you simplicity: single discount tier applied to aggregate tokens, then we apply a region factor (EU: +2%, APAC: +7%) to the blended per-token rate for invoice reporting.
- Weighted buckets give better control: excess over a regional allocation is billed at the next lower tier but can be rebalanced with one-off recredits each quarter.
- Retroactive credits: we can provide limited retroactive credits for the first quarter of a contract if the variance is <20% from the forecast; larger variances handled on a case-by-case.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call early next week with procurement + engineering to lock the billing model and pilot terms. Are you available Mon/Tue?

Attachments: [proposed-geo-pricing-notes.pdf (pdf)]

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: Elena Soto <esoto@atlasai.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing question — region splits & commit pooling

Elena — quick follow from the pricing desk. Two concrete items to clarify: 

1) Metering and cross-region math (example):
- If AtlasAI commits $2,000,000 / year and we assume an average blended per-token list price of $0.00012 before discounts, a 10% commit discount produces an effective base of $0.000108.
- Apply regional multipliers for invoicing: US x1.00, EU x1.02, APAC x1.07. So APAC effective per-token would be ~$0.0001156 after multipliers.
- If you want no APAC surcharge, we can price APAC at US rates but require a dedicated regional capacity addendum (sunk infra uplift) in the SOW.

2) Commit flexibility: 
- Option A (blended): single commit, single set of tiers, invoice shows per-region multipliers. Simpler operationally.
- Option B (weighted): allocate the commit across regions (e.g., US=$1.2M, EU=$600k, APAC=$200k) with an automatic quarterly rebalancing policy and one recredit per quarter for variance >5%.

We can also offer an introductory credit equal to one month of average usage tokens for pilots under $50k/mo usage. If you want that built into the term sheet I can add an explicit credit line.

HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/ATLAS-2025-Q3

— Rafael
Rafael Mendes | Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Rafael — that math helps. A couple follow-ups after reviewing with procurement: 

- Can you confirm whether credits (pilot credit or recredit) are applied as an invoice-level line item or as token-bucket adjustments in the control plane? Procurement prefers invoice credits for visibility.
- APAC question: given our latency-sensitive inference in APAC, we may route those calls to a regional endpoint hosted by a partner — would Redwood still apply the APAC surcharge if we host through a local partner?
- Can the commit start date be backdated to the pilot start (we sometimes start billing cohorts earlier than contract signature)?

Attached updated usage by endpoint and a CSV with monthly token estimates for Q3.

Attachments: [usage_breakdown_2025Q2.csv (csv)]

—Elena

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com, AtlasAI Procurement <procurement@atlasai.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing question — region splits & commit pooling

Elena — quick technical + commercial note to address the APAC routing question: 

- If AtlasAI sends traffic to Redwood's hosted APAC endpoints (managed by Redwood): APAC surcharge applies (standard +7% on effective per-token after discounts) because of cross-region infra costs.
- If you host inference with a certified local partner or run Redwood Private in-region: we can waive the surcharge but require a small regional capacity reservation (typically expressed as a $/mo uplift) to cover reserved infra. This would be in the SOW.
- Billing mechanics: credits are applied as invoice-level line items by default (procurement-friendly). We can also show token-bucket adjustments in the console for operational visibility.
- Commit backdating: we can backdate a commit up to 30 days prior to the signed start date if the pilot is signed off and usage is within forecast; exceptions handled with legal approval.

Proposed short MAP (mutual action plan):
1) Pilot kickoff (2 weeks): pilot config + 30k token pilot credit applied to first invoice.
2) Billing model sign-off (week 3): choose Blended vs Weighted buckets.
3) SOW/DocuSign (week 4): finalize APAC uplift/dedicated clause and signature.

DocuSign term sheet: https://www.docusign.com/agreements/ABCD-ATLAS-TERM-SHEET

If that looks good, Lauren and I will draft the final term summary for procurement.

— Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni | Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
